title: Giardiniera Smash Sausage Hoagies
seoTitle: Giardiniera Smash Sausage Hoagies | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Smash sausage night—flat-top char, pepper onions, not smoked links
subtitle: Smashed Italian sausage, charred peppers, and onion hoagies for ten
description: Italian sausage links smash flat on the griddle until crisp, griddle with peppers and onions, and serve on toasted rolls with marinara dip.

steps.title: Prep sausage for smash
steps.instruction: Remove sausage from casings or use loose bulk sausage formed into patties. Have smashing spatula ready. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Use giardiniera relish, beef tallow, fennel pollen, Calabrian chili paste as listed — measure each before heat goes on. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Slice peppers and onions
steps.instruction: Cut peppers and onions into uniform strips for even griddle char. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F with a 3-minute rest on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Preheat the flat-top griddle
steps.instruction: Preheat griddle to 425°F. Film with oil. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Smash and griddle sausage
steps.instruction: Place sausage on griddle and smash flat immediately. Cook 4 minutes per side until charred and 165°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Griddle peppers and onions
steps.instruction: Griddle pepper-onion mix at 425°F until charred and tender, 8–10 minutes. Season with oregano and pepper flakes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold at 170°F
steps.instruction: Chop smashed sausage and hold with peppers and onions covered at 170°F. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Toast rolls
steps.instruction: Toast sub rolls cut-side down at 375°F until crisp. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Line for ten
steps.instruction: Pile sausage and pepper mix on rolls with optional provolone melt. Marinara on the side for dipping. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

proTips: Smash within 10 seconds of hitting the griddle—cold sausage won't spread.
Casings removed or bulk sausage smashes flatter than linked sausage.
Marinara dip on the side keeps rolls from going soggy during hold.
tonightSpread: Griddle smash sausage and pepper hoagies.
leftovers: Sausage mix into pasta with marinara.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Smashed sausage cooks faster than whole links and builds more crust. Distinct from smoked sausage-pepper trays—this is pure flat-top char.
mealPrepNotes: Smash sausages at 425°F, 4 minutes per side. Griddle peppers and onions alongside. Hold covered at 170°F up to 40 minutes. Rolls toast at 375°F.
